title: Topology-aware token shard synchronizer for heterogeneous GPU pools
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Problem: In mixed customer workloads we observe high tail latency and underutilized NIC/NVLink bandwidth when tensor- and pipeline-parallel stages are mapped to heterogeneous GPU topologies (NVLink meshes + PCIe islands). Current token routing assumes uniform device bandwidth and uses global batching windows that cause frequent NCCL stalls during prefill and decode handoffs.

Goal: Implement a topology-aware token shard synchronizer in the runtime scheduler that: (1) maps logical token shards to device-local preferred lanes based on measured bandwidth/latency; (2) staggers prefill->decode rendezvous per-device to maximize NCCL overlap without increasing median latency; (3) exports lightweight kernel-selection hints (sequence-length and kv-cache locality) so device runtimes can pick attention kernels and fusions that avoid blocking communication.

Constraints: Must be backwards-compatible with existing model placement policies and not require model re-sharding at model-load time. The synchronizer should be a soft layer in the conductor scheduler so it can be toggled and A/B tested. It must operate with limited telemetry (per-request seq_length, device BW estimate, recent NCCL stall metrics).
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end scheduler honors per-device topology map and creates shard assignments that reduce average NCCL stall time by >=20% on our heterogeneous cluster testbed (see perf harness).
Tail p99 latency for mixed short+long sequence workloads improves by >=15% for prefill+decode compared to baseline scheduling.
Kernel-selection hint path implemented: scheduler publishes per-request 'kv-locality' and 'expected-length' flags; device runtime uses them to select attention kernels without semantic changes.
Feature guarded behind runtime flag and rollout can be limited to a specific region or customer tier.
Comprehensive unit and integration tests covering topology changes, transient device failures, and scaling from 2->32 GPUs added to CI harness.
work_items: design topology descriptor and device scoring function (bandwidth, connectivity, historical stall rate)
implement shard assignment algorithm that minimizes cross-island NCCL traffic using greedy partition + local smoothing
add scheduler API for per-request kernel-selection hints (kv_locality, expected_seq_length_bucket)
modify prefill rendezvous to emit stagger offsets per-device based on shard placement
integrate metrics for NCCL stall time, per-stage wait time, and shard imbalance; expose in Console dash
end-to-end perf runs on dedicated cluster (A100 NVLink mesh + PCIe fallback) with production trace replay
safety: rollout flag, rollback path, and canary tests (small % of traffic)
docs: design note in Confluence, runtime flag docs, and changelog entry for runtime-1.20
comments: 2026-02-21 Marco Ruiz: Kickoff — sketched scoring function for NVLink vs PCIe; initial thought is to prefer local NVLink groups for hot-kv shards and spread cold shards across islands.

2026-02-25 Aisha Patel: Prototype shard assignment completed in scheduler simulator. Microbench shows 12% NCCL stall reduction on synthetic waveforms but only 4% on prod traces — likely due to sequence length correlation across requests.
2026-03-01 Rahul Mehra (review): Questioned the heuristic tie-breaker when devices have similar scores. Suggested adding 'recent stall slope' to prefer devices that have improving NIC queues.

2026-03-04 Aisha Patel: Added kernel-selection hint path (expected_seq_length_bucket & kv_locality boolean). Device runtime PR created to switch to fused attention kernel when kv_locality==true and seq_length<256.

2026-03-08 Perf run: Mixed short/long trace (prod-replay v3) executed on 8xA100 (NVLink groups of 4). Results: NCCL stall time reduced 23%, p99 prefill+decode latency improved 17%, throughput neutral (+2%). Attaching raw numbers to design doc.
2026-03-10 Security review: team asked to confirm hints do not leak sensitive request metadata. Confirmed hints are aggregated enums and do not contain tokens or prompt fragments.
2026-03-11 PM note (Leah Kim): Roadmap alignment — schedule for runtime-1.20; coordinate with Dedicated capacity team for reserved pool validation.
notes: Decision: shard assignment will be computed per-request group (requests that share model+version) with a lightweight LRU device score cache to avoid costly recompute.
Trade-off: greedy partitioning minimizes immediate cross-island traffic but can lead to imbalance; we add local smoothing step (move smallest hot shards to underutilized devices) to mitigate.
Implementation detail: use 8-length seq_length buckets (0-32,33-64,...,>1024) for hint granularity — reduces cardinality in telemetry and stays useful for kernel choice.
Rollback: scheduler flag 'topo_shard_sync_v1' controls both assignment and hint emission; disabling the flag falls back to legacy global windows and removes hints.
Metrics to track post-rollout: per-request NCCL stall percent, p50/p95/p99 prefill latency, shard imbalance ratio (max/min token-per-device over rolling 5m).
Next steps: polish canary thresholds, add failure injection tests (kill one NVLink link, simulate high PCIe latency), and coordinate Console dashboard for early-warning alerts.
